page: Amazon Web Services t9g.nano is an entry-level burstable instance in the General Purpose family, utilizing arm64 AWS Graviton processors managed by the AWS Nitro System. The hardware allocation delivers 2 dedicated vCPUs from 2 physical cores clocked at 3.3 GHz, running with a single thread per core. System memory is sized at 0.5 GB, establishing an allocation density of 0.25 GB per core. The instance includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for the operating system and user data.

The compute profile is governed by a burstable performance baseline. With a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps and limited RAM, system throughput relies on burst allowances rather than sustained resource availability. The dual physical cores provide dedicated execution on 64-bit ARM hardware, but the 0.5 GB memory footprint restricts runtime environments from hosting memory-intensive runtimes or dense process trees.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, t9g.nano offers minimal overhead for tasks requiring negligible steady-state compute. Tradeoffs include strict memory constraints and the absence of ephemeral storage. The instance fits lightweight workloads such as low-traffic bastion hosts, simple health-check services, automated cron jobs, and minimal monitoring agents.
